Sara / Orbit team —

Thanks for the note. Per Jonas, Redwood's commercial intent is prospective-only. Below is proposed redline text for Exhibit B that we believe removes the ambiguity and provides a clear operational true-up for mid-cycle ramps. We also included a short example to make sure both sides align.

Proposed Exhibit B amendment (redline snippet):
"Section 3(b) — Usage-triggered Floor Reset (amended):

When Customer's measured usage in any billing period meets or exceeds a Threshold as defined in the Pricing Schedule, Redwood will apply a Floor Reset. The Floor Reset is prospective: any change resulting from the Floor Reset shall apply to subsequent billing periods only and shall not alter charges already invoiced for closed billing periods. For avoidance of doubt, in months that span multiple billing cycles (e.g., Customer ramps mid-month), Redwood will calculate the Floor Reset on the aggregate usage for the completed billing cycle and apply any new floor or rate to the following billing cycle.

True-up procedure for split-cycle ramp:
• If a Floor Reset is triggered mid-month, Redwood will not retroactively reprice tokens already invoiced for the partial billing period.
• Redwood will compute the adjustment at the next invoice as an additive true-up (line item) that reflects the delta between the old and new floor for usage consumed after the reset effective date, limited to a reconciliation window of fourteen (14) days following Redwood's issuance of the applicable invoice.

Example (illustrative only):
• Billing period A (May 1–May 31): usage through May 20 = 900k tokens; threshold = 1M tokens. On May 22, cumulative usage hits 1M tokens (trigger). Under this amendment the new floor and rates apply to June 1–June 30. No retroactive adjustment will change the May invoice that has already been issued. If a prorated adjustment is required for billing systems that split invoices, Redwood will compute a single additive true-up on the next invoice covering any delta and will accept disputes within the 14-day reconciliation window.

If Orbit prefers a shorter or longer reconciliation window, we can discuss — our standard is 14 days but we've made exceptions for larger enterprise billing flows.

We can produce a redlined Exhibit B doc and send for e-signature once you confirm the amendment language. Proposed change preserves commercial predictability (no retroactive repricing) while giving Orbit a clear reconciliation path.
